title: IDEA: A Flexible Framework of Certified Unlearning for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Trained graph neural networks may encode sensitive personal information from graph data, creating a risk of privacy leakage when deployed.

gap.claim: Existing certified unlearning methods for graph neural networks mostly handle only node and edge requests and are typically limited to specific GNN designs or training objectives, reducing their flexibility.

contributions.claim: Proposes IDEA, a framework for flexible and certified unlearning for graph neural networks.
Instantiates four types of graph unlearning requests and proposes an approximation approach for handling them across diverse GNNs.
Provides a theoretical guarantee of the proposed approach's unlearning effectiveness as a certification.

stated_novelty.claim: Unlike existing alternatives, IDEA is not designed for a specific GNN or optimization objective and is intended to generalize easily.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate IDEA's superiority across multiple key perspectives.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks are widely deployed, while their training data may contain sensitive personal information.
Sensitive information can be encoded in trained GNN parameters and exposed through privacy leakage.
Certified machine unlearning provides theoretical removal guarantees, but existing methods have narrow request coverage and limited architectural or objective flexibility.
IDEA combines four graph unlearning request types with a flexible approximation approach and a theoretical certification.
The authors characterize IDEA as generalizable and report superiority in extensive real-world dataset experiments.

source_observation.claim: Existing certified unlearning approaches are often specialized to particular GNN designs or training objectives.

interpretation.claim: Unlearning flexibility can be limited by coupling the method to model architecture or optimization choices.

application.claim: When designing graph unlearning methods, target support across multiple request types, GNN architectures, and training objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the proposed flexibility holds for all GNNs, objectives, or request types beyond the stated four.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four unlearning request types.
The abstract does not describe the approximation procedure or theoretical guarantee.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
